expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: | (SubscriptionBase & { status: "trialing"; trialEndDate: Date }) | ... — status is the discriminant across all variants

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Each intersection in the union adds only its own fields; trialing has only trialEndDate, active only renewalDate, etc.

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: assertNever function provided; used in describe switch with default: return assertNever(sub)

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionId, CustomerId, PlanId all branded using Brand<T, B> pattern

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states this doesn't cover and leaves it to user; mentions isValidTransition but doesn't provide it

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Lists 4 specific misuses: ID swapping, bag-of-optionals nonsense, silent undefined reads, new status not breaking build

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary design is discriminated union; explicitly rejects optionals throughout
